$ openssl verify -CAfile root-ca/cert.pem -untrusted int-ca-ecc/cert.pem pay-edge/cert.pem
pay-edge/cert.pem: OK

$ openssl x509 -in root-ca/cert.pem -noout -text | grep -E 'Public-Key|Signature Algorithm'
        Signature Algorithm: sha256WithRSAEncryption
                Public-Key: (4096 bit)
    Signature Algorithm: sha256WithRSAEncryption
$ openssl x509 -in pay-edge/cert.pem -noout -text | grep -E 'Public-Key|Signature Algorithm|ASN1 OID'
        Signature Algorithm: ecdsa-with-SHA256
                Public-Key: (256 bit)
                ASN1 OID: prime256v1
    Signature Algorithm: ecdsa-with-SHA256

--- s_client at default seclevel (1) against pay-edge (ECDSA P-256) ---

--- s_client with cipherstring forcing @SECLEVEL=4 (192-bit minimum) against the same P-256 cert ---
$ openssl s_client -connect 127.0.0.1:8443 -tls1_2 -cipher "ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256:@SECLEVEL=4" -brief
Connecting to 127.0.0.1
907D0000:error:0A0000B5:SSL routines:ssl_cipher_list_to_bytes:no ciphers available:../openssl-3.5.4/ssl/statem/statem_clnt.c:4176:No ciphers enabled for max supported SSL/TLS version

pay-edge/cert.pem: OK

-- Re-recorded 2026-09-27 (ecdat-harness PKI bump; NOT_BEFORE moved to
2026-09-27, see ecdat-harness/README.md "Deterministic PKI" -> "Bumping the
PKI" and docs/open-issues.md OI-019). Ran against a local `openssl s_server
-accept 8443 -cert pay-edge/cert.pem -key pay-edge/key.pem -cert_chain
int-ca-ecc/cert.pem -www` (openssl 3.5.4, Git Bash /mingw64/bin/openssl.exe),
started/stopped for this recording only; no s_server left running. The
verify-error text differs slightly from the original 2026-09-26 capture
("unable to get local issuer certificate" at depth=1 vs. the earlier
two-line depth=0 "unable to verify the first certificate") because this run
served the chain via `-cert_chain` explicitly rather than a single combined
PEM; the substantive result (handshake succeeds at default seclevel,
correctly refused once ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256 is combined with
@SECLEVEL=4, chain verifies OK) is unchanged.
